headline: High: n8n can execute commands and write files while ingesting Khoj outputs, creating dangerous default-path automation and data-flow risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj can surface indexed notes/docs and optional web search content, while n8n can consume workflow inputs and route them into downstream nodes. There is no documented shared channel by default, but if Khoj output is copied into n8n or passed through a workflow, prompt-like content could steer automation. The pathway is plausible, not proven blocked.
conditions: IF Khoj-generated text is inserted into an n8n AI Agent or Code node without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF n8n workflows treat retrieved note content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer actions.
mitigations: Add a fixed system prompt that forbids executing instructions from retrieved content.
Insert a manual review step before any n8n node that acts on Khoj text.
Strip markdown, links, and imperative phrases from Khoj outputs before workflow use.
Use a separate workflow branch for untrusted text.
requires-engineering: implement provenance tagging from Khoj into n8n.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, and n8n can read/write the server filesystem plus send data through many integrations. If Khoj outputs are routed into n8n workflows, sensitive note content can flow into external services or logs. The pair does not show a built-in shared workspace, so this is a default-workflow leakage risk rather than a guaranteed leak.
conditions: IF a workflow forwards Khoj note content into an external n8n integration, that content leaves the local note boundary.
IF n8n logging is enabled on workflows handling Khoj data, sensitive text may be retained in logs.
mitigations: Disable verbose execution logging for workflows handling notes.
Mask or redact note content before sending to integrations.
Use a dedicated n8n credential and workspace for Khoj-related flows.
Review each node’s output mapping before enabling the workflow.
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction in the workflow.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj is read-only on the filesystem, but n8n has execute_shell and write_filesystem enabled, so the pair can overlap on the same files if connected through a shared workspace or workflow. Because n8n can mutate server state and run commands, concurrent use can overwrite or corrupt artifacts that Khoj indexes. Uncertainty about the exact shared path escalates this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF n8n writes to files that Khoj indexes, Khoj may read partially updated or inconsistent content.
IF both agents operate on the same directory without locking, file races can corrupt artifacts.
mitigations: Separate Khoj-indexed directories from n8n working directories.
Disable Execute Command for workflows that touch shared files.
Add file-locking around any shared path.
Run a quick audit for overlapping paths in both configs.
requires-engineering: introduce transactional writes for shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can generate answers from retrieved documents, and n8n’s AI Agent/workflow nodes can treat upstream text as actionable input. If n8n uses Khoj output as authoritative without verification, a mistaken or manipulated retrieval can cascade into automated downstream actions. Because n8n has execution authority, the blast radius is larger than a simple misquote.
conditions: IF n8n routes Khoj answers directly into action nodes, errors can become automated actions.
IF no verification step exists between Khoj retrieval and n8n execution, hallucinations or stale facts can propagate.
mitigations: Require a human approval step before action nodes.
Add a verification node that checks Khoj outputs against source documents.
Limit n8n to read-only notifications until validation passes.
Log source citations alongside every Khoj-derived claim.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds for auto-execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj is explicitly for personal notes and indexed documents, while n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and stores credentials on its server. If personal or regulated notes are routed into n8n, retention and residency controls may diverge from the source system’s expectations. The profiles do not prove a specific legal mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated notes are sent into n8n workflows, the workflow’s retention and logging settings must match the source policy.
IF n8n stores workflow execution data longer than Khoj retains notes, compliance mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Check retention settings for the relevant n8n workflows.
Avoid sending regulated notes into third-party integrations.
Purge old execution histories for sensitive workflows.
Document the data flow and retention owner.
requires-engineering: align retention/deletion policies across both systems.
